evidence: src/application/orders/ChangeOrderStatusUseCase.ts: execute() loads the order through requireOrder(this.orders, ...) and saves it with this.orders.save(order), which is orchestration through repository ports
order.transitionTo(target, this.clock.now()) hands the state-transition rules to the domain entity
stockEffectOf(target) lets the domain value-object module decide the stock effect
this.stock.commit / this.stock.release hand the stock allocation work to the domain StockAllocator
TARGET_STATUS turns the command's OrderAction into a domain OrderStatus, which is application-level command translation
toOrderDto(order) does output mapping, an application concern
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file does use-case orchestration, which is the application layer's job. The business rules stay in domain code. The order's own transitionTo method enforces state transitions, the domain function stockEffectOf decides what each status means for stock, and the domain StockAllocator does the stock commit and release. Loading and saving go through repository interfaces, and the current time comes from an injected Clock port. The file has no persistence, transport or framework code. The TARGET_STATUS table only turns the command's action into the target domain status, which is ordinary application-level command handling. The branch on `effect` just sends the work to the right domain service method based on the result the domain returned; it adds no business rule of its own. Mapping to a DTO with toOrderDto is also an application concern.
